## Motivation

The Automations dialog mixed repository details, loading text, and validation across several surfaces, which made Cloud setup noisy and allowed unsupported repository ownership to fail only at creation time. This PR streamlines repository selection, checks repository-owner eligibility when the repository changes, and consolidates dialog feedback into one accessible notification center.

## Changes made

- Hide public repositories, keep owner/repository details in hover text, and show repository-setting checks beside the selected repository.
- Disable the Owner control until repository-owned creation is confirmed, with the unsupported reason available through hover and accessible descriptions.
- Centralize informational, warning, and error feedback in a neutral notification center with semantic outlines and icons.
- Keep Cloud model and tool configuration available, hide the harness picker, and normalize unsupported Weekdays schedules to Manual.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The call path and cardinality are explicit: `GitHubRepositoryFetcher.getRepositories` requests up to 100 results and maps `repository.private` to `IGitHubRepository.isPrivate`; this loop discards that field and calls `isRepositorySelectable`; that method awaits `repositories.get` before `automations.getConfiguration`. The updated test itself observes five metadata requests before the first batch is released. Cache hits can remove repeat work, but a cold search is definitively affected.
Findings.PerformanceResource: GitHub repository metadata network calls and their response bytes.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The added request count grows linearly with cold search results (up to 100 per search); execution is capped at five candidates, but batches are awaited sequentially and each private candidate chains metadata then capability requests.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased repository-picker latency and excessive network I/O/API usage on cold searches.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Each cold search candidate incurred only the automation capability request, in bounded groups of five. Privacy was already present in the search response but was not separately re-fetched.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Repository search now performs a repository-metadata network read for every candidate and, for private repositories, then performs the prior automation-capability read serially.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: At RIGHT line 193, the search loop changed from `store.isRepositoryManageable(...)` to `store.isRepositorySelectable(...)`. The latter newly calls `client.repositories.get(repository, signal)` before the existing `client.automations.getConfiguration(...)`, even though each `repository` returned by `getRepositories` already has `isPrivate`.
Findings.Title: Reuse search privacy instead of refetching every repository
Findings.Impact: Opening or typing in Add Repository can make up to 100 unnecessary GitHub metadata requests and force each private-repository batch through two serial network round trips, delaying repository results and consuming API quota.
Findings.Evidence: `IGitHubRepository` includes `isPrivate`, populated directly by `GitHubRepositoryFetcher.toGitHubRepository`. `getRepositories` asks GitHub for up to 100 results. The changed loop processes groups of five and awaits each whole group before starting the next. `isRepositorySelectable` issues `client.repositories.get` for every cold key, then issues `getConfiguration` for private keys. `cloudAutomationStore.test.ts` now expects `metadataRequestsBeforeRelease: 5`, directly proving the added per-candidate boundary calls.
Findings.Recommendation: Filter public results using `repository.isPrivate` before batching, then retain the existing manageability check for private candidates (or pass/seed the known privacy into the store). This preserves privacy filtering and cache semantics without a second metadata request per result.

Scenarios.Scenario: Search for and add a GitHub repository from the Cloud automation workspace picker
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Authentication and the GitHub repository search complete first; then every five-item eligibility batch must complete before the next starts, and all batches must complete before results are returned to the picker. For each cold private result, metadata completes before capability checking starts.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per picker opening before search.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same authentication occurred before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks opening the authenticated repository search flow.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch up to 100 repositories, including privacy metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per search invocation at this layer; a nonempty query transitively performs authenticated-user, organization-list, and repository-search requests, while an empty query lists authenticated repositories.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same search ran and already returned `isPrivate` for each result.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks eligibility filtering and result display.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refetch metadata for each candidate with `client.repositories.get`.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One per cold result, up to 100, despite privacy already being present in the search result; cached keys avoid repeats.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each five-item batch waits for these calls, and private candidates cannot begin capability checks until they finish.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read Cloud automation configuration/manageability for private candidates.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One per cold private result after metadata, up to 100; groups of five candidates are processed at a time.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One capability read occurred for every cold candidate, without a preceding metadata round trip.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks completion of the current batch and therefore picker results.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of cold repository results after search, up to 100; net added calls equal the number of private results, while all results incur the redundant metadata operation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Repository candidates are grouped into sequential batches of five. Within a batch, up to five metadata requests run concurrently; each private result then starts its capability request. There is no shared in-flight coalescing across simultaneous consumers.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold repository keys miss account-lifetime privacy/manageability maps. Successful privacy and manageability results are cached by normalized repository key; failures use bounded LRU retry timestamps. Warm repeated results avoid the per-result checks, but the initial GitHub search request still runs. Concurrent misses are not coalesced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: result privacy, the changed call path, sequential awaits, batch size, cache keys, and test-observed request counts are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact private/public mix, cache hit rate, network RTT, and frequency of cold searches vary. The API limit of 100 and serial batch structure establish the upper bound and latency mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable high-severity network boundary fan-out: known privacy is discarded and re-read per candidate, adding up to 100 calls and a serial round trip for private-result batches.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or switch the automation dialog to Cloud mode and evaluate recent workspaces
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The dialog renders while checks run, but affected repository rows remain pending and target-dependent save/selection progress waits for eligibility. The watcher initiates checks for all recent workspaces so filtering can occur before the visible recent limit.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve a recent local/remote workspace to a GitHub repository reference.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per cold recent workspace target.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Precedes remote eligibility checks; implementation-specific resolution may use provider state, but no diff-added filesystem/subprocess boundary was established.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch repository metadata to determine privacy.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One per cold resolved recent target, subject to the five-task limiter.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Eligibility went directly to the capability request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Private targets wait for this before capability checking; public targets stop here.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch automation manageability configuration for private repositories.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One per cold private recent target.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One request occurred for every resolved target, including public repositories.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Completes target eligibility and unblocks the row/save path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: All recent candidate workspaces observed in Cloud mode, including entries beyond the final ten visible rows until privacy filtering is known.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A shared target eligibility limiter allows five tasks. For each resolved private repository, metadata and capability calls are sequential.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: `targetEligibility` caches by workspace URI for the account/client lifetime. Privacy and manageability are cached by repository key and reset on account/client invalidation, but the initial `getWorkspaceTarget` task performs its own reads; failures remain represented in the target observable until explicit clearing/reset.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the eager watcher, limiter, and sequential network path are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of stored Git recent workspaces and private/public mix vary. The checks are limited to five concurrent tasks and target observables prevent repeat work for the same URI during the account lifetime.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding: this is a real added cold-path cost, but unlike search the recent-workspace objects do not already expose privacy; concurrency and lifetime caching bound the required policy check. The redundant-search finding addresses the clearly avoidable fan-out.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render and interact with automation dialog feedback, loading indicators, owner/schedule controls, and mobile caption
Scenarios.CriticalPath: DOM updates occur synchronously on form validation, target/tool observable changes, owner activation, save failure, and Cloud connection state. They do not cross subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network boundaries beyond target/tool operations covered separately.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: User interaction and observable update frequency; state cardinality remains fixed.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: UI callbacks are serialized on the renderer event loop; asynchronous Cloud operations retain their existing cancellation/observable ownership.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No remote cache is involved. Notification rendering keeps the last source/severity/text/action tuple and skips unchanged DOM updates; message state is bounded to seven fixed sources and disposed with the dialog.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed code scans seven message priorities and performs guarded class/text/icon updates.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact validation event frequency varies with user input, but work per update is constant and bounded.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The notification center and spinner work are bounded constant-size DOM operations, and unchanged notification tuples are explicitly suppressed.

Scenarios.Scenario: Filter and hover ActionList repository rows
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Filtering is synchronous on text input; hover focus restoration performs constant-size DOM focus/containment checks and list focus updates.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of action-list items times filter keystrokes; realistic repository lists are at most 100 from this provider path.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single renderer event loop; no asynchronous fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache or expensive boundary. Filtering computes lowercase label, description, and optional `filterText` for each currently supplied item on each filter evaluation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the filter loop and hover handlers are directly changed.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: List size varies, but repository search is capped at 100 and the added operation is one lowercase/substring check per visible candidate.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The added string match is linear with the existing filtering pass and does not introduce a costly boundary, retained state, layout loop, or meaningful UI-thread amplification.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create a repository-owned automation and translate unsupported-ownership failure
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A single create mutation remains on the save critical path. The new catch only inspects the returned error and maps one known message; it issues no retry or preflight request.

ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same single create request occurred; the raw error propagated on failure.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks successful dialog completion, as before.

Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing mutation sequencer serializes store writes; no new concurrency is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new cache. The mutation follows the existing store sequencing and account-lifetime cancellation behavior.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Mutation latency depends on the service, but call count and scheduling are unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance finding; error translation adds only constant local work and no boundary calls.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 16 changed files and all diff pages. One high-confidence boundary-fan-out regression was reported for redundant per-result repository metadata requests in Cloud repository search. UI rendering, action-list filtering, recent-target eligibility, mobile presentation, and create error translation were traced and did not yield additional actionable performance regressions.
